prompt: Zero-rated supplies count towards the AED 375,000 mandatory VAT registration threshold.
options: True
False

explanation.what: Zero-rated supplies are taxable supplies taxed at 0%, so they count towards the registration thresholds. Exempt supplies don't.
explanation.why: A business selling only zero-rated exports can still pass AED 375,000 and have to register. Thinking that 0% means it doesn't count confuses zero-rated supplies with exempt ones, which are left out.
explanation.reference: Federal Decree-Law No. 8 of 2017, Article 13; VAT Executive Regulation, Article 7

meta.reviewNotes: Approved by the team; confirmed by Wahaj on 8 Nov 2026.

prompt: A business finds that its taxable supplies over the past 12 months have passed AED 375,000. How long does it have to apply for VAT registration?
options: 7 days
30 days
90 days
Until the end of the calendar year

explanation.what: A business that becomes required to register must apply to the tax authority within 30 days.
explanation.why: Passing AED 375,000 on a rolling 12-month basis triggers mandatory registration, and the application is due within 30 days. Waiting until the year end is wrong because the test isn't tied to the calendar year, and 7 and 90 days aren't the deadline.
explanation.reference: Federal Decree-Law No. 8 of 2017, Article 13; VAT Executive Regulation, Article 8

meta.reviewNotes: Confirm the article that sets the 30-day application deadline (Exec. Reg. Art. 8 recalled). | Approved by the team; confirmed by Wahaj on 8 Nov 2026.

scenario: Lagoon Breeze Interiors LLC was set up in Dubai last month and hasn't made any sales yet. It has just signed a contract to fit out a hotel lobby for AED 520,000 before VAT. The work, the invoicing and the payment will all happen within the next 30 days.
prompt: What is Lagoon Breeze's VAT registration position?
options: It needn't register until it has 12 months of sales history.
It can only register voluntarily, because it has no past supplies.
It must register now, because it expects its supplies in the next 30 days to exceed AED 375,000.
It must register only once the customer has paid.

explanation.what: Registration is mandatory if taxable supplies passed AED 375,000 over the past 12 months, or are expected to pass it in the next 30 days.
explanation.why: Lagoon Breeze expects AED 520,000 of taxable supplies within the next 30 days, which is over AED 375,000, so the forward-looking test is met now. A new business doesn't need a sales history, and the obligation doesn't wait for payment.
explanation.reference: Federal Decree-Law No. 8 of 2017, Article 13; VAT Executive Regulation, Article 7

meta.reviewNotes: Approved by the team; confirmed by Wahaj on 8 Nov 2026.

prompt: A business that makes only zero-rated supplies can apply to the tax authority to be excepted from VAT registration.
options: True
False

explanation.what: A taxable person whose supplies are all zero-rated may apply for an exception from registration, even if it passes the threshold.
explanation.why: All its supplies are taxed at 0%, so it would owe no output VAT anyway, and the law lets it ask to be excepted. If it takes the exception it can't recover input tax through VAT returns, which is why some zero-rated businesses choose to register anyway.
explanation.reference: Federal Decree-Law No. 8 of 2017, Article 15

meta.reviewNotes: Confirm Art. 15 wording, and that the business must notify the tax authority if it starts making standard-rated supplies. | Approved by the team; confirmed by Wahaj on 8 Nov 2026.

prompt: When a business checks whether it has passed the AED 375,000 registration threshold, it must include the sale of one of its capital assets, such as its old delivery van.
options: True
False

explanation.what: Sales of capital assets are left out when working out the value of supplies for the registration threshold.
explanation.why: The threshold measures a business's regular trading. A one-off sale of a capital asset, such as a van used in the business, is excluded from the calculation, so it can't on its own push the business over AED 375,000.
explanation.reference: Federal Decree-Law No. 8 of 2017, Articles 13 and 19

scenario: Over the past 12 months, Oasis Thread Tailoring LLC made standard-rated sales of AED 200,000 and zero-rated exports of AED 150,000. It also received AED 90,000 of exempt rent from letting a flat it owns to a family. It made no imports and expects no big change in the next 30 days.
prompt: What is Oasis Thread's VAT registration position?
options: It must register, because its income of AED 440,000 is over AED 375,000.
It isn't required to register, because its taxable supplies are AED 350,000, but it may register voluntarily.
It isn't required to register and can't register voluntarily, because only AED 200,000 is standard-rated.
It must register, because any business that exports goods must register.

explanation.what: Taxable supplies, including zero-rated ones, count towards the thresholds; exempt supplies don't. Registration is mandatory above AED 375,000 and voluntary registration is possible above AED 187,500.
explanation.why: Taxable supplies are AED 200,000 + AED 150,000 = AED 350,000, which is under AED 375,000, so registration isn't required. That is above AED 187,500, so it may register voluntarily. Adding the exempt rent to reach AED 440,000 is the tempting mistake.
explanation.reference: Federal Decree-Law No. 8 of 2017, Articles 13 and 17; VAT Executive Regulation, Article 7

meta.reviewNotes: Approved by the team; confirmed by Wahaj on 8 Nov 2026.

scenario: Over the past 12 months, Qamar Ridge Bakery LLC made standard-rated sales in the UAE of AED 180,000 and zero-rated exports of AED 90,000. It also imported baking equipment and ingredients for its business worth AED 120,000, which would have been standard-rated if bought in the UAE. Its only other income was AED 50,000 of exempt residential rent.
prompt: Does Qamar Ridge have to register for VAT?
options: No. Only its UAE sales of AED 270,000 count, so it may register voluntarily.
No. Exports and imports don't count, which leaves AED 180,000.
Only if its supplies in the next 30 days alone go over AED 375,000.
Yes. Its taxable supplies and imports total AED 390,000, which is over AED 375,000.

explanation.what: The mandatory threshold counts taxable supplies, including zero-rated ones, plus imports that would be taxable if supplied in the UAE. Exempt supplies are left out.
explanation.why: AED 180,000 + AED 90,000 + AED 120,000 = AED 390,000, which is AED 15,000 over the threshold, so it must register. Leaving out the imports gives AED 270,000, the tempting wrong answer. The exempt rent is rightly not counted.
explanation.reference: Federal Decree-Law No. 8 of 2017, Article 13; VAT Executive Regulation, Article 7

meta.reviewNotes: Approved by the team; confirmed by Wahaj on 8 Nov 2026.

scenario: Nordwind Gadgets GmbH is based in Germany and has no place of business in the UAE. It keeps stock in a third-party warehouse in Dubai and sells gadgets from it to private individuals who order online, delivering within the UAE. Its UAE sales are about AED 200,000 a year.
prompt: Does Nordwind need to register for UAE VAT?
options: Yes. A non-resident must register, whatever its sales, when it makes taxable supplies in the UAE and no one else has to account for the VAT on them.
No. Its sales are under the AED 375,000 mandatory threshold.
No. Its customers account for the VAT under the reverse charge.
No. A business with no place of business in the UAE is outside UAE VAT.

explanation.what: A non-resident making taxable supplies in the UAE must register regardless of the threshold if no other person has to account for the VAT on those supplies.
explanation.why: The gadgets are in the UAE and delivered there, so the place of supply is the UAE. The buyers are private individuals, so nobody can account for the VAT under the reverse charge. That leaves Nordwind, which must register even though its sales are only about AED 200,000.
explanation.reference: Federal Decree-Law No. 8 of 2017, Article 13; VAT Executive Regulation, Article 7

meta.reviewNotes: Confirm the article and paragraph for non-resident registration irrespective of the threshold. | Approved by the team; confirmed by Wahaj on 8 Nov 2026.

prompt: Under the general rule in UAE VAT law, where is a supply of services made?
options: Where the customer has its place of residence
Where the supplier has its place of residence
Where the contract is signed
Where the payment is received

explanation.what: Unless a special rule applies, a supply of services is made where the supplier has its place of residence.
explanation.why: The general rule looks at the supplier. Special rules override it for cases such as services connected with real estate, transport, restaurants and hotels, events, and services a UAE-registered business receives from abroad. The customer's location matters only under those special rules.
explanation.reference: Federal Decree-Law No. 8 of 2017, Article 29

meta.reviewNotes: Confirm Art. 29 as the general place-of-supply rule for services. | Approved by the team; confirmed by Wahaj on 8 Nov 2026.

prompt: Services connected with real estate, such as an estate agent's services, are supplied where the property is located.
options: True
False

explanation.what: Services connected with real estate are supplied where the property is, whoever and wherever the supplier and customer are.
explanation.why: This special rule overrides the general rule based on the supplier's residence. An agent's services for a flat in Dubai are supplied in the UAE even for an overseas client, and services for a property abroad are supplied abroad.
explanation.reference: Federal Decree-Law No. 8 of 2017, Article 30

meta.reviewNotes: Confirm the Art. 30 paragraph and that estate agency (brokerage) services are covered. | Approved by the team; confirmed by Wahaj on 8 Nov 2026.

prompt: Dhow Line Logistics LLC, in Dubai, trucks a customer's goods from Jebel Ali to a warehouse in Fujairah. How is this transport service treated for VAT?
options: Zero-rated, as a transport service
Exempt, as local transport
Standard-rated at 5%, because it is transport within the UAE
Outside the scope of UAE VAT

explanation.what: Transport services are supplied where the transport begins. Only international transport is zero-rated, and the local transport exemption covers passengers, not goods.
explanation.why: The trip starts in Dubai and ends in Fujairah, so the place of supply is the UAE and the transport isn't international: 5% applies. The exemption for local transport covers carrying passengers, so it doesn't help here.
explanation.reference: Federal Decree-Law No. 8 of 2017, Articles 30, 45 and 46

meta.reviewNotes: Confirm the Art. 30 paragraph for transport services. | Approved by the team; confirmed by Wahaj on 8 Nov 2026.

scenario: Bluewave Pool Services LLC, in Ras Al Khaimah, sells three pool pumps to a hotel in Nairobi, Kenya. It ships them to Nairobi, and its engineers install them at the hotel.

In the UAE, because Bluewave is based there, so 5% is due
In the UAE, because the pumps were shipped from there, so 5% is due
In the UAE, but the supply is exempt

explanation.what: When goods are supplied with installation or assembly, the place of supply is where they are installed or assembled.
explanation.why: The pumps are installed at the hotel in Nairobi, so the place of supply is Kenya, outside the UAE, and no UAE VAT is charged. The tempting answers look at where Bluewave is based or where the goods were shipped from, which this special rule overrides.
explanation.reference: Federal Decree-Law No. 8 of 2017, Articles 27 and 28 (place of supply of goods)

In the UAE, where the services are used and enjoyed
In the UAE, and the customers account for the VAT under the reverse charge
Outside the scope of UAE VAT, because the supplier has no UAE presence

It is supplied in Kenya, where it is performed, so no UAE VAT is due
5%, because the trainers travelled from the UAE

explanation.why: If the goods are delivered first, delivery is the earliest event, so it fixes the date of supply. A payment received later doesn't move it.

October–December, because the laptops were delivered on 3 October
October–December, because payment arrived on 20 October
Either return, as Sandstone chooses

explanation.why: The invoice on 25 September comes before delivery (3 October) and payment (20 October), so the date of supply is 25 September and the VAT goes in the July–September return. The supplier can't choose.

scenario: Bluewave Pool Services LLC has a year-long maintenance contract with a villa compound and bills it every quarter. For one quarter, it issues the tax invoice on 25 March with payment due on 10 April. The customer pays on 8 April.

25 March, when the tax invoice was issued
10 April, the due date on the invoice
The last day of the quarter the work covers

scenario: Desert Oven Engineering LLC sells an oven to Qamar Ridge Bakery LLC for AED 210,000 including VAT. Desert Oven files quarterly returns for July–September and October–December. It receives a 20% deposit of AED 42,000 on 20 September, delivers and invoices the oven on 5 November, and is paid the balance on 30 November.
prompt: How much output VAT should Desert Oven report in each return?
options: AED 10,000 in October–December only
AED 2,100 in July–September and AED 8,400 in October–December
AED 2,000 in July–September and AED 8,000 in October–December
AED 2,000 in July–September and AED 10,000 in October–December

explanation.what: A payment received before delivery or invoicing fixes the date of supply for the amount paid. The VAT inside a VAT-inclusive amount is amount × 5/105.
explanation.why: The AED 42,000 deposit includes VAT of 42,000 × 5/105 = AED 2,000, due in July–September. Total VAT is 210,000 × 5/105 = AED 10,000, so AED 8,000 remains for October–December, on delivery. Taking 5% of each amount (2,100 and 8,400) overstates the VAT; AED 10,000 in the second quarter counts the deposit twice.
explanation.reference: Federal Decree-Law No. 8 of 2017, Article 25

meta.reviewNotes: Approved by the team; confirmed by Wahaj on 8 Nov 2026.
